land.text: the Gold Coast Colony, Ashanti and the Northern Territories: 'On 6 March 1957, the Colony of Gold Coast gained independence as the state of Ghana.'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's British Gold Coast row runs 1943-1959 and again as a 1960 shape, and is a 1.19 M km2 composite (modern countries Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon), so it overlaps Ghana's own shape in 1958-1959.

land.text: the former Trust Territory of Togoland under British administration, merged with the Gold Coast at independence; 'Volta Region ... includes much of the former mandate's territory'

predecessors.note: British Togoland has no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet.

capitals.name: Accra
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Accra'. The Gold Coast page gives Accra as the colony's capital from 1877 (infobox) after Cape Coast, so the seat does not change at independence.

correction.text: Ghana's 1958 shape, applied from independence on 6 March 1957: 'the Gold Coast, Ashanti, the Northern Territories, and British Togoland were unified as one single independent dominion'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Ghana row begins in 1958 but independence, and the union with British Togoland, were on 6 March 1957. Cliopatria's British Gold Coast row (1943-1959) still draws the land in 1957 and 1958-1959; the integrator should end that row's claim on Ghana in March 1957.

240,673 km2 for 1958-1959 against the Ghana article's 239,567 km2 in the text (the infobox says 240,000 and a further paragraph 238,540; no year): ratio 1.00. This is the whole of present-day Ghana including the Volta Region, as the Gold Coast page puts it: 'The borders of present-day Ghana were realised in May 1956 when the people of the Volta region' voted.

240,844 km2 for the single year 1960, the same land as 1958-59 (0.07 percent larger, grid noise). Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960 ('Nkrumah declared Ghana a republic and assumed the presidency'), a rename event, not a border change.

240,759 km2 for 1961-2023, the same land: the Ghana page describes no border dispute or territorial change after 1957 ('shares borders with Ivory Coast to the west, Burkina Faso to the north, and Togo to the east').

region.text: the Gold Coast Colony, Ashanti and the Northern Territories as one dominion; British Togoland (the Volta Region) joins by the gain event of the same day

ledger.note: 1957: the Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana, the first colony in Sub-Saharan Africa to do so. 'On 6 March 1957, the Colony of Gold Coast gained independence as the state of' Ghana; infobox 'Independence as the Dominion of Ghana: 6 March 1957'. [Reviewer af-08-f, 2026-10-19: region written as Ghana minus the Volta Region, as in the predecessor land, so that the British Togoland gain of the same day is not counted twice.]

region.text: British Togoland, the former Trust Territory of Togoland under British administration

ledger.note: 1957: British Togoland is united with the new Ghana. The plebiscite of 9 May 1956 gave '58% of the voters taking part' for merging with the Gold Coast; the union was 'with effect from midnight 6 March 1957'. The Gold Coast page's infobox dates 'Incorporation of British Togoland' to 11 December 1956 and the UN resolution recommending union is 13 December 1956; the Ghana and British Togoland pages use 6 March 1957. The Volta Region is the researcher's reading of 'much of the former mandate's territory'.

1960: Ghana becomes a republic with Nkrumah as president. 'Nkrumah declared Ghana a republic and assumed the presidency.' The 1 July date is the fetch summary's reading of the page. Same state, same land (rule 2).

certainty.note: Colonial treaty and survey lines: the Northern Territories boundaries 'were demarcated in 1898 and 1899' against French and German colonies; British Togoland's western edge is the plebiscite line of 1956 (the Volta Region). No page opened describes a dispute over the land boundary after 1957.

notes: Cliopatria: four Ghana shapes 1958-2024 at 240,673-240,844 km2 on one bbox (the 1960 and 1961-2023 shapes differ by under 0.1 percent: grid noise); the row starts a year late (independence 6 March 1957) and the 1957 keyframe is new. Overlap to resolve: Cliopatria's British Gold Coast row (1943-1959; 1960 shape of 954,027 km2) is a 1.19 M km2 composite across Nigeria, Ghana and Cameroon and still covers Ghana in 1957-1960; the Gold Coast was not a colony after 6 March 1957. Counterparts needing dossiers: british-togoland (the Trust Territory under British administration, 1916 to 6 March 1957, the page gives 27 December 1916 as admission and 1919 as the link to the Gold Coast); a French Togoland / togo dossier exists in af-08. No war, dispute or border change after 1957 appears on the three pages opened, so wars is empty; the 2012 ITLOS maritime case with Ivory Coast and the Ewe unification question were not on the pages and are not recorded. No ruler strip: the Ghana article dates Nkrumah (1957-1966), Kufuor (7 January 2001), Mahama (24 July 2012), Akufo-Addo (7 January 2017) but not the intervening reigns. Native name: none on the page.
